name: Boris Spassky
milestone_by_age_26: Won the World Junior Chess Championship and earned the Grandmaster title in 1955 at age 18, then qualified for the Candidates Tournament at 19.
early_history_summary: Spassky learned chess at age 5 while evacuated from besieged Leningrad during WWII. He joined the Leningrad Palace of Pioneers chess club at age 10 under coach Vladimir Zak, who provided sustained training and even fed him during postwar poverty. By 15 he placed second at the Leningrad Championship, and by 18 he was a Grandmaster and World Junior Champion.
family_context_summary: Father served in the military; mother was a schoolteacher. Family lived in poverty in postwar Leningrad; parents divorced. His grandfather was a prominent Russian Orthodox priest and State Duma deputy.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of chess expertise in the family; Spassky's entry into chess was self-directed, discovered during wartime evacuation.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet chess pipeline, Palace of Pioneers, dedicated coach, wartime adversity
evidence_summary: Spassky benefited from the Soviet Union's elite chess development pipeline, joining the Palace of Pioneers at age 10 where coach Vladimir Zak provided sustained individualized training, stipends, and even food during postwar poverty. By 18 he was a Grandmaster and World Junior Champion, qualifying for the Candidates Tournament at 19. His family was impoverished after the war and his parents divorced, but the Soviet chess system provided a structured path to elite competition. His grandfather had been a State Duma deputy and priest, but there was no chess lineage in the family.

name: A. R. Rahman
milestone_by_age_26: Composed the debut film score for Mani Ratnam's Roja (released July 1992) at age 25, winning the National Film Award for Best Music Direction.
early_history_summary: Rahman began studying piano at age 4 under his father R.K. Shekhar, a film score composer for Malayalam cinema. After his father's death when Rahman was 9, he played keyboards professionally from age 12 to support his family, working in recording sessions for years before transitioning to advertising jingles and then film scoring with Roja in 1992.
family_context_summary: Father R.K. Shekhar was a film score composer and conductor for Malayalam films who died when Rahman was 9, forcing the family into financial hardship. Rahman's mother used Shekhar's industry connections to get the young Rahman work in recording sessions.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Father was film composer, early studio access, financial hardship, keyboard prodigy, Indian film industry
evidence_summary: Rahman's father R.K. Shekhar was a film score composer for Malayalam cinema, providing direct domain exposure and studio access from age 4. After Shekhar's death when Rahman was 9, the family faced severe financial hardship, and Rahman's mother leveraged Shekhar's industry connections to get the boy work as a keyboard player at recording sessions from age 12. This gave him roughly 13 years of professional studio experience before his breakthrough with Roja at 25. The adversity of losing his father and needing to support his family created urgency and deep immersion in the craft.

name: Gylmar dos Santos Neves
milestone_by_age_26: Starting goalkeeper for Corinthians, winning three Campeonato Paulista titles (1951, 1952, 1954), and debuted for the Brazil national team in 1953 at age 22.
early_history_summary: Gilmar began his career at hometown club Jabaquara, joining their youth setup in 1945 at age 15. He moved to Corinthians in 1951 at age 21 and immediately won the Campeonato Paulista, becoming a starting goalkeeper. He earned his first Brazil cap in 1953 and was a South American Championship runner-up the same year.
family_context_summary: Named after his parents Gilberto and Maria. Born in Santos, São Paulo. Family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Brazilian football pipeline, Corinthians, early professional debut
evidence_summary: Gilmar grew up in Santos, a major footballing city, and joined local club Jabaquara's youth system at 15. He moved to Corinthians at 21 and became a starting goalkeeper, winning three state titles by 24. His Brazil national team debut came at 22 in 1953. Family background is not well documented, but the Brazilian football pipeline provided a clear path from local clubs to top-tier professional play. He was later voted best Brazilian goalkeeper of the 20th century.

name: Hank Marvin
milestone_by_age_26: As lead guitarist of The Shadows, scored a UK #1 hit with 'Apache' in 1960 at age 19, establishing himself as Britain's first guitar hero with multiple chart-topping instrumentals through his early twenties.
early_history_summary: Marvin began playing banjo and piano as a teenager in Newcastle, taught by a school music teacher who sold him a banjo. At 16 he moved to London in April 1958, met Cliff Richard's manager at the 2i's Coffee Bar in Soho, and joined Cliff Richard's backing band (the Drifters, later The Shadows). By 1960 The Shadows had a #1 hit with 'Apache.'
family_context_summary: Father was an army officer. Family was not wealthy; Marvin's parents could not afford banjo lessons so he taught himself from a book. His father bought him a guitar for his 16th birthday.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of musical background in the family; Marvin's interest in music was self-directed, inspired by BBC radio and Buddy Holly.
primary_early_advantage_tags: London 2i's Coffee Bar, skiffle movement, Cliff Richard, early British rock and roll
evidence_summary: Marvin grew up in Newcastle with no family musical background; his father was an army officer and the family could not afford music lessons. He taught himself banjo from a book and formed a skiffle group at school. The critical advantage was moving to London at 16 in 1958, during the birth of British rock and roll, where he landed at the 2i's Coffee Bar in Soho—a key talent discovery venue. Joining Cliff Richard's backing band provided immediate national distribution and platform. His partnership with school friend Bruce Welch was also significant. The Shadows' 'Apache' hit #1 in the UK in 1960 when Marvin was 19.

name: Nicolaas Bloembergen
milestone_by_age_26: Published first physics paper at age 20 (1940), and by 26 was a graduate assistant at Harvard working on nuclear magnetic resonance with Purcell and Pound, co-authoring papers in Physical Review (1946).
early_history_summary: Bloembergen entered the University of Utrecht in 1938 and published his first paper in Physica at age 20. He completed his master's equivalent and doctoral qualifying exams by 1943 under German occupation, then traveled to Harvard in 1946 where he joined Purcell and Pound's NMR research group as a graduate assistant, co-authoring seminal Physical Review papers.
family_context_summary: Father was a chemical engineer and executive at a chemical fertilizer company. Mother held an advanced degree to teach French. Maternal grandfather was a high school principal with a Ph.D. in mathematical physics. Family was middle-class and well-educated.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Utrecht University, Harvard, Purcell NMR group, educated family, Dutch academic system
evidence_summary: Bloembergen came from an educated family—his father was a chemical engineer, his mother held an advanced teaching degree, and his maternal grandfather had a Ph.D. in mathematical physics. He entered the University of Utrecht at 18 and published his first paper at 20. The Dutch academic system's emphasis on independent study allowed him to complete his doctoral qualifying exams by 1943 despite wartime occupation. His father financed his passage to Harvard in 1946, where he arrived six weeks after the NMR discovery and was immediately accepted as a graduate assistant by Purcell and Pound. This placed him at the frontier of a major scientific wave, co-authoring Physical Review papers by age 26.

name: James Watson
milestone_by_age_26: Co-discovered the double helix structure of DNA with Francis Crick, published in Nature on April 25, 1953, at age 25—one of the most consequential scientific discoveries of the 20th century.
early_history_summary: Watson entered the University of Chicago at 15 on a tuition scholarship, earned his B.Sc. in zoology at 19, and his Ph.D. from Indiana University at 22 under Salvador Luria. After a postdoctoral year in Copenhagen, he joined the Cavendish Laboratory at Cambridge in 1951 where he met Crick and began the collaboration that led to the DNA double helix discovery.
family_context_summary: Father was a businessman; mother's father was a Scottish-born tailor. Raised in Chicago. The family was not wealthy but Watson received a tuition scholarship to the University of Chicago's gifted youngster program at 15.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of scientific background in the family. Watson's father was a businessman. His interest in biology began with bird-watching as a child, shared with his father.
primary_early_advantage_tags: University of Chicago gifted program, Indiana University, Cavendish Lab, Salvador Luria, Francis Crick, phage group
evidence_summary: Watson was a precocious student who entered the University of Chicago at 15 through a gifted youngster program, benefiting from an elite institutional pipeline. He was mentored by Salvador Luria at Indiana University (a pioneer in phage research) and then placed at the Cavendish Laboratory at Cambridge through Luria's network. His partnership with Francis Crick was a high-trust complementary collaboration that directly led to the DNA double helix discovery. The phage group and Cavendish Lab placed him at the frontier of molecular biology, a major structural wave in science. Family was middle-class; no scientific lineage, but the educational pipeline was the key accelerator.

name: Tony Scott
milestone_by_age_26: Made BFI-funded directorial debut 'One of the Missing' (1968) at age 24, followed by the BFI-funded feature 'Loving Memory' (1970) at age 26, which screened at the Cannes Film Festival.
early_history_summary: Scott studied art at West Hartlepool College of Art, Sunderland Art School, and the Royal College of Art, following his older brother Ridley. He made his directorial debut with the BFI-funded short 'One of the Missing' (1968) at 24, then 'Loving Memory' (1970) at 26 with BFI and Albert Finney funding, before joining Ridley's commercial production company.
family_context_summary: Father was a Colonel in the Royal Engineers. The family was working-class in northern England. Tony was the youngest of three sons; his brother Ridley Scott, six years older, became a major film director and paved the way for Tony's career in the arts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Ridley Scott, Royal College of Art, BFI Production Board, Albert Finney funding
evidence_summary: Tony Scott's primary early advantage was his older brother Ridley Scott, who had already established a path into filmmaking through art school and the Royal College of Art. Tony followed the same educational route and benefited from Ridley's network and production company. The BFI Production Board provided competitive funding for his first two films. A grand-uncle, Dixon Scott, was a pioneer of cinema chains in Tyneside. The family was working-class but the Scott brothers' mutual support and shared path into commercial filmmaking was the key accelerator. Tony's later fame came with Top Gun (1986) at age 42, but his BFI-funded early films represent a material milestone by 26.

name: Morgan Freeman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Freeman graduated high school in 1955, joined the U.S. Air Force, then studied acting in the early 1960s. His professional theater debut came in 1967 at age 30, and fame arrived with The Electric Company (1971) at age 34.
early_history_summary: Freeman began acting in school plays at age 9 and won a statewide drama competition at 12, but turned down a drama scholarship to join the Air Force. After leaving the military, he studied acting in Los Angeles and San Francisco in the early 1960s. By 26 he was still a struggling student actor with no professional credits.
family_context_summary: Son of a barber and a teacher. Raised in low-income households in Mississippi and Chicago under Jim Crow-era conditions.
evidence_summary: Freeman showed early acting talent, winning a statewide drama competition at 12, but chose to join the Air Force after high school instead of pursuing acting. He did not begin professional acting training until his early twenties, and his professional theater debut did not come until 1967 at age 30. By 26, he had no material, independently verifiable milestone in acting.

name: Toto Cutugno
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Cutugno was a working musician playing drums in local bands and touring Italy by his early twenties, but his songwriting breakthrough came in the 1970s and his biggest hit 'L'Italiano' arrived in 1983 at age 40.
early_history_summary: Cutugno began playing drums at age 7 and formed his first band 'Toto e i Tati' at 19. He toured with Guido Manusardi's jazz ensemble and played in local bands through his twenties, but had no notable recordings or chart success by age 26.
family_context_summary: Father was a Sicilian sea marshal who played trumpet; mother was a housewife. Family moved to La Spezia shortly after his birth. Not wealthy; Cutugno received a diploma in accounting instead of formal music education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father played trumpet recreationally, which exposed Cutugno to music, but there is no evidence of professional music industry connections or formal training in the family.
evidence_summary: Cutugno showed early musical interest, playing drums from age 7 and forming bands as a teenager, but by age 26 he was still a working musician without any notable recordings, chart hits, or awards. His songwriting career took off in the 1970s when poet Vito Pallavicini noticed him, and his major successes (Sanremo, Eurovision, 'L'Italiano') came well after age 26. No material, independently verifiable milestone was found by age 26.

name: Svetlana Alliluyeva
milestone_by_age_26: No material writing milestone by age 26 found. Alliluyeva graduated from Moscow University in 1949 at age 23 and began teaching, but her first book 'Twenty Letters to a Friend' was published in 1967 at age 41, following her defection to the West.
early_history_summary: As Stalin's daughter, Alliluyeva grew up in the Kremlin with immense privilege but also extreme personal turmoil—her mother committed suicide when she was 6, and her father sent loved ones to the gulag. She graduated from Moscow University in 1949 and taught Soviet literature and English, but had no published writing by 26.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Joseph Stalin and his second wife Nadezhda Alliluyeva, who committed suicide in 1932. Grew up with immense political privilege but also severe personal trauma and isolation within the Soviet system.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was the dictator of the Soviet Union; this provided political privilege but no literary or writing domain advantage. Her writing career emerged from her unique personal story, not from family literary tradition.
evidence_summary: Alliluyeva was born into extraordinary political privilege as Stalin's daughter, but this did not translate into a material writing milestone by age 26. She graduated from Moscow University at 23 and taught literature and English, but her writing career only began after her defection to the West in 1967 at age 41. Her fame as a writer comes from her memoirs about growing up as Stalin's daughter, not from any literary achievement by 26. No material, independently verifiable writing milestone was found by age 26.

name: Kenzaburō Ōe
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Akutagawa Prize in 1958 at age 23 for the short story 'The Catch' (Shiiku), Japan's most prestigious literary award for emerging writers, while still a university student.
early_history_summary: Ōe grew up in a remote village on Shikoku island, raised on oral traditions from his grandmother. At 18 he moved to Tokyo and enrolled in French Literature at the University of Tokyo. He started writing in 1957 at age 22, won the Tokyo University May Festival Prize, and the following year won the Akutagawa Prize at 23, launching his professional literary career.
family_context_summary: Born into a landowning family in a remote village on Shikoku. His father had a bark-stripping business and died in 1944 during the Pacific War. His mother became the driving force behind his education, buying him books including Huckleberry Finn and The Wonderful Adventures of Nils.
parent_family_domain_summary: No literary tradition in the family, but the Oe clan had deep roots in the village with oral storytelling traditions passed down by women. His mother was instrumental in his education and literary development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: University of Tokyo, French literature, Akutagawa Prize, oral storytelling tradition, postwar Japanese literature
evidence_summary: Ōe grew up in a remote village with a rich oral storytelling tradition passed down by his grandmother, which deeply influenced his writing. His mother, widowed during the war, actively supported his education with books. The key institutional advantage was attending the University of Tokyo to study French Literature under Professor Kazuo Watanabe, which gave him both literary training and access to Japan's literary establishment. He started writing at 22 and won the Akutagawa Prize at 23, transitioning directly from student to professional writer. The postwar Japanese literary scene provided a structural wave of opportunity for new voices.

name: Kevin Costner
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Costner graduated from CSUF in 1978, worked in marketing, and became a stage manager at Raleigh Studios. His film debut in the small nonunion picture 'Stacy's Knights' came in 1981 at age 26, but his breakthrough arrived with 'The Untouchables' (1987) at age 32.
early_history_summary: Costner was not academically inclined and discovered acting relatively late. He earned a business degree from CSUF in 1978, took acting lessons on the side, and worked odd jobs including marketing and as a stage manager at Raleigh Studios before getting small film roles in the early 1980s.
family_context_summary: Father was an electrician and utilities executive; mother was a welfare worker. Middle-class family. Costner has English, Irish, Scottish, Welsh, and Cherokee ancestry.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of entertainment industry connections in the family. Costner's interest in film was self-directed, inspired by watching movies as a child.
evidence_summary: Costner had a late start in acting, earning a business degree before pursuing acting lessons on the side. By 26 he was working as a stage manager at Raleigh Studios with only a tiny nonunion film debut. His breakthrough came at 32 with The Untouchables (1987). A chance encounter with Richard Burton on an airplane inspired him to commit fully to acting, but this happened after age 26. No material, independently verifiable milestone was found by age 26.
